questions.question: 1. What is the primary aim of the experiment described in the text?

answers.a: To measure the maximum transmit power of a base station.
answers.b: To understand how various factors affect the downlink Carrier-to-Interference ratio.
answers.c: To calculate the exact path loss exponent for a city.
answers.d: To design a new type of cellular antenna.

questions.question: 2. What does 'Tx power of B.S.' refer to?

answers.a: The processing speed of the base station.
answers.b: The amount of signal strength the base station transmits.
answers.c: The power consumed by the base station's cooling system.
answers.d: The total number of users connected to the base station.

questions.question: 3. Which objective relates to the concept of using the same frequencies in different, separated cells?
4. What is 'sectoring' used for in a base station?

answers.a: To divide a cell into multiple directional segments to reduce interference.
answers.b: To connect the cell to different parts of the core network.
answers.c: To increase the physical height of the base station tower.
answers.d: To assign different frequencies to every single user.

answers.a: The change in signal strength due to the time of day.
answers.b: The signal blockage caused by large obstructions like buildings or hills.
answers.c: The interference from adjacent frequency channels.
answers.d: The pattern of radio waves cast by the antenna itself.

questions.question: 6. How might changing the 'B.S. height' impact the cell?

answers.a: It only changes the power consumption of the base station.
answers.b: It only affects the path loss exponent.
answers.c: It can alter the cell's coverage area and its interference with other cells.
answers.d: It has no significant effect on signal propagation.

questions.question: 7. What does the 'path loss exponent' parameter represent?

answers.a: The rate at which signal strength decreases with distance.
answers.b: The total number of paths a signal can take.
answers.c: The power level of the transmitted signal.
answers.d: The physical angle of the antenna.

questions.question: 8. What is the purpose of adjusting the 'vertical beam tilt' of an antenna?

answers.a: To aim the signal more towards the ground or the horizon.
answers.b: To change the frequency of the signal.
answers.c: To physically rotate the antenna horizontally.
answers.d: To switch the antenna between transmit and receive modes.

questions.question: 9. The experiment aims to study the 'downlink' C/I ratio. What does 'downlink' refer to?

answers.a: The communication from the mobile phone to the base station.
answers.b: The communication from the base station to the mobile phone.
answers.c: The connection between two different base stations.
answers.d: The signal that has been lost due to shadowing.

questions.question: 10. According to the text, how might a teacher guide this experiment?

answers.a: By asking students to build their own base station.
answers.b: By having students write a new path loss formula.
answers.c: By limiting the variables to test, such as focusing only on Tx power.
answers.d: By removing all parameters except frequency reuse.
